Minutes from the Fed's last meeting come out Wednesday. ![Image 1: Stephen Alpher](https://www.coindesk.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.sanity.io%2Fimages%2Fs3y3vcno%2Fproduction%2F9c64385838f127845d0783e09a18548c2b886ce2-512x512.png%3Fw%3D64%26h%3D64%26fit%3Dcrop%26crop%3Dfocalpoint%26auto%3Dformat&w=96&q=75) ## Nasdaq and S&P 500 close at record highs The gains were modest —the Nasdaq rising 0.5% and the S&P 500 0.6% — but it was enough for the two major U.S. stock indexes to close at new record highs. While the Nasdaq has been making new highs regularly, it was the S&P’s first all-time close in two months. The Mag 7 names were broadly higher, though Meta slipped a hair. There was also strength in recently beaten-down consumer names and utilities as interest rates took a rare move lower. Crypto prices continued their recent flatlining action, with bitcoin, ether, XRP, and solana all little changed over the past 24 hours. * * * ![Image 2: Stephen Alpher](https://www.coindesk.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.sanity.io%2Fimages%2Fs3y3vcno%2Fproduction%2F9c64385838f127845d0783e09a18548c2b886ce2-512x512.png%3Fw%3D64%26h%3D64%26fit%3Dcrop%26crop%3Dfocalpoint%26auto%3Dformat&w=96&q=75) ## 'Coping' as bitcoin continues to flatline “‘The longer the base, the higher the space’ is the appropriate cope while waiting for bitcoin’s next range breakout,” [writes Brian Brookshire](https://x.com/btc_overflow/status/2107528569836724245). Brookshire writes as bitcoin at $85,500 continues to trade in a narrow range for about the fourth consecutive week
